solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Very naughty boy admitting deed arrived with large animal (8,5)

indicatorNotes.admitting: the boy's name lets the deed in
indicatorNotes.with: the pieces for 'arrived' and L sit side by side

blocks.note: Brian, of Monty Python's Life of Brian: 'he's a very naughty boy'; split B…RIAN

annotation.surface: A badly behaved boy owns up to something he did on arrival with a big beast.
annotation.walkthrough: 'large animal' reads as one phrase, but 'large' is only the L and 'animal' alone is the definition. The naughty boy quotation is from Life of Brian.
annotation.definitionFit: The two-humped camel of central Asia is a specific animal, so the definition is by category.

entries.clue: Magmatic rock in house on fire in Somerset location (9)

indicatorNotes.in: the house and fire pieces go inside the Somerset city

blocks.note: Bath is a city in Somerset; split BAT…H

annotation.surface: A house burns down in Somerset, set on volcanic rock.
annotation.walkthrough: Bath is a Roman spa city in the English county of Somerset.
annotation.definitionFit: A batholith is a huge mass of igneous rock that cooled from magma deep underground.

entries.clue: Endorse business millions put back together (7)

blocks.note: to mend is to put something back together

annotation.surface: A firm backs a merger that brings millions back together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'put back' looks like a reversal instruction, but the whole phrase 'put back together' simply means mend.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to praise something publicly is to put your name behind it.

entries.clue: Informer at Oxford University damaging end of satellite dish (11)

indicatorNotes.end of: only the final letter of 'satellite' is used

annotation.surface: A spy at Oxford sabotages the end of a satellite dish.
annotation.walkthrough: 'satellite dish' reads as one aerial; the break comes before 'dish', which is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Ratatouille is a Provençal dish of stewed vegetables.

entries.clue: Authority surrounding vineyard to increase due to natural growth (6)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: the word for authority goes around the vineyard

blocks.note: an ace is an expert, an authority; split AC…E
a cru is a vineyard, as in grand cru

annotation.surface: An official body takes over a vineyard so it can grow its yields.
annotation.walkthrough: 'to increase' reads as one verb, but 'to' is the link and the definition starts at 'increase'.
annotation.definitionFit: Interest or benefits accrue when they build up gradually over time.

entries.clue: Plots from prisoners in steeple — on the contrary (9)

indicatorNotes.in: read literally, prisoners go inside the steeple
indicatorNotes.on the contrary: swap the roles: the steeple goes inside the prisoners

annotation.surface: Escape plans hatched by convicts hiding in a church tower.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses the container: the spire goes inside the cons, not the cons inside the spire.
annotation.definitionFit: Conspires means plots together in secret.

entries.clue: Range Patschke initially displayed in warped materialism (8,4)

indicatorNotes.initially: take only the first letter of Patschke
indicatorNotes.displayed in: that letter joins the rest of the fodder
indicatorNotes.warped: the letters are bent out of shape

annotation.surface: An artist named Patschke shows work criticising a warped obsession with money.
annotation.walkthrough: Patschke is there only for its P; the name sounds like a painter to fit 'displayed'.
annotation.definitionFit: The Maritime Alps are the mountain range at the south-western end of the Alps, by the Mediterranean.

entries.clue: Beauty forsaken keeping cool (10)

indicatorNotes.keeping: the word for forsaken holds the word for cool

annotation.surface: An abandoned beauty stays cool.
annotation.walkthrough: 'cool' reads as calm, but it means fashionable, which gives IN.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the quality of being lovely is beauty.

entries.clue: Renaissance work, perhaps in red, almost ruined (3,6)

indicatorNotes.ruined: the letters of 'red almost' are wrecked and rebuilt

annotation.surface: A Renaissance painting, done in red, has been nearly destroyed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'almost' reads as modifying 'ruined', but it is part of the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: An old master is a painting by a great European artist of roughly 1500 to 1800.

entries.clue: Beastly noise reason tattooist must stop? (4)

blocks.note: a tattooist stops when the ink runs out: zero (O) plus the dye

annotation.surface: A tattooist halts work because a client squealed.
annotation.walkthrough: The second half is a pun: O INK, zero ink, is the reason a tattooist has to stop.
annotation.definitionFit: By example: the grunt of a pig is the beastly noise meant.

entries.clue: In which an education is not nearly completed? (8,8)

annotation.definition: In which an education is not nearly completed?

blocks.note: a course of study, taken at face value
the surface says barely finished; the setter means finished not near, i.e. from far away

annotation.surface: A complaint about a course that never quite gets finished.
annotation.walkthrough: 'not nearly' reads as 'far from finished', but it means done from far away, by correspondence or online.
annotation.definitionFit: Distance learning is studying remotely, without attending the institution in person.

entries.clue: At sea stop son boarding a vessel (5)

indicatorNotes.boarding: the son gets on, into the vessel

blocks.note: a vat is a vessel for liquid; split VA…T

annotation.surface: At sea, a son is stopped from getting on board a ship.
annotation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, and at sea it would be; here it is a vat.
annotation.definitionFit: Avast is a sailors' command meaning stop.

entries.clue: Viscous mixture doubled energy in sauce (7)

indicatorNotes.doubled: the word for viscous mixture is written twice

blocks.note: tar, a thick black mixture, twice

annotation.surface: A sticky mixture with a double dose of energy goes into a sauce.
annotation.walkthrough: 'in' reads as part of the recipe; it only links wordplay and definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Tartare sauce is mayonnaise with capers and gherkins, served with fish.

entries.clue: What large wave did affected stable situation (6,3,4)

blocks.note: literally: a big wave rocks a boat
the idiom: to disturb a settled state of affairs

annotation.surface: A big wave upsets a calm scene.
annotation.walkthrough: One reading is literal seafaring, the other the idiom for causing trouble.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom read literally: a wave really does tip a vessel, and the phrase means upsetting a settled state.

entries.clue: Attract agency employee with training at first (5)

indicatorNotes.at first: only the opening letter of training

blocks.note: a temp is a worker placed by an agency

annotation.surface: Luring a temp by offering training first.
annotation.walkthrough: A temp is a temporary office worker supplied by an employment agency.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lure or entice someone is to attract them.

entries.clue: Disputes in short stories about Poe’s visitor (11)

indicatorNotes.about: the stories go around the visitor

blocks.note: contes are short tales, from French; split CONT…ES
the raven that visits the narrator in Poe's poem The Raven

annotation.surface: Arguments in a collection of short stories about Edgar Allan Poe.
annotation.walkthrough: Poe's visitor is the raven in his poem, which comes 'tapping at my chamber door'.
annotation.definitionFit: To contravene a claim is to dispute or contradict it.

entries.clue: Golden openings for athletes using roids in competition (5)

indicatorNotes.openings for: take the first letter of each following word

blocks.note: first letters of Athletes Using Roids In Competition

annotation.surface: Gold medals are won by athletes on steroids.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Golden openings' suggests golden opportunities; 'Golden' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Auric means of or like gold.

entries.clue: Clear behind, go higher still at bridge (9)

annotation.surface: Someone clears the rear to climb higher on a bridge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'bridge' reads as a structure to climb; it is the card game.
annotation.definitionFit: To overtrump is to play a higher trump card than one already played.

entries.clue: Mythical creature doing away with king’s charge (4)

blocks.note: R = rex, king, is taken out

annotation.surface: A troll does away with the king's charge.
annotation.walkthrough: 'king's' looks possessive of 'charge', but it is the R being removed and the definition is 'charge' alone. A troll under the bridge also exacts tolls.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a fee paid to use a road or bridge is a charge.

entries.clue: Hard boarding transport in Hannibal’s birthplace (8)

indicatorNotes.boarding: the H gets on, into the transport word

blocks.note: cartage is transport by cart; split CART…AGE

annotation.surface: Getting hard on board transport in Hannibal's home town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'transport' reads as a vehicle but here it is the charge or act of carrying: cartage.
annotation.definitionFit: Hannibal was born in Carthage, the ancient city in modern Tunisia.

entries.clue: Toothless mammal in garden, say, hiding head (8)

indicatorNotes.hiding head: the first letter is concealed, i.e. removed

blocks.note: STATE (to say) minus its first letter

annotation.surface: A toothless animal lurking in a garden with its head hidden.
annotation.walkthrough: 'say' is a verb to be turned into STATE, not the usual 'for example'.
annotation.definitionFit: An edentate is a mammal of the group once including sloths and anteaters, with few or no teeth.

entries.clue: Indiana university beset by dull element (6)

indicatorNotes.beset by: the university letter is surrounded by the word for dull

annotation.surface: A university in Indiana is hemmed in by something dull.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Indiana university' reads as one institution, but IN and U are separate pieces.
annotation.definitionFit: Indium is a soft silvery metallic element.

entries.clue: Show for workers a month before vacuous redeployment (9,7)

indicatorNotes.vacuous: empty the word of its insides, keeping only its outside letters

annotation.surface: A show put on for workers a month before a pointless redeployment.
annotation.walkthrough: 'before' is a piece meaning 'once', not an order instruction. The Proms in London are promenade concerts.
annotation.definitionFit: A promenade concert is a concert where some of the audience stand, as at the BBC Proms.

entries.clue: Darkness close — close to what? (5)

annotation.surface: Darkness is falling, but close to what?
annotation.walkthrough: The same word 'close' is used twice in two senses: near, then end.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the hours without daylight are the darkness.

entries.clue: Militant on Severn dressed in green (16)

indicatorNotes.dressed: the letters are dressed, i.e. arranged, into a new order

annotation.surface: A protester by the river Severn, dressed all in green.
annotation.walkthrough: 'green' reads as a colour of clothing; it is the noun for an environmental campaigner. The Severn is Britain's longest river.
annotation.definitionFit: A green is a supporter of environmental causes, an environmentalist.

entries.clue: Anticyclone comes down in mountainous region (9)

blocks.note: an anticyclone is a high-pressure system, a high

annotation.surface: Weather settles over the mountains.
annotation.walkthrough: A weather forecast in Britain calls an anticyclone simply a high.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, best known from the mountainous north of Scotland.

entries.clue: Joker — nameless criminal? (7)

indicatorNotes.nameless: the N for name is taken out

annotation.surface: The Joker as an anonymous villain, as in Batman.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface nods at the Batman villain; 'Joker' is simply a comedian.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: someone who tells gags is a joker.

entries.clue: Country roads run back past a club (7)

indicatorNotes.back: the roads and run are read backwards
indicatorNotes.past: going past something puts you ahead of it, so the A comes first

annotation.surface: Country lanes leading back past a football ground.
annotation.walkthrough: LANES+R turned round gives RSENAL, with A placed in front. Arsenal is a London football club.
annotation.definitionFit: A proper name by example: a famous London football club.

entries.clue: Elevated construction beginning to bend in strong wind (5)

indicatorNotes.beginning to: only the first letter of bend
indicatorNotes.in: that letter goes into the wind

blocks.note: a gale is a strong wind; split GA…LE

annotation.surface: A tall building starts to bend in a gale.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Elevated construction' suggests a whole tower; it is the triangle of wall under a roof's peak.
annotation.definitionFit: A gable is the raised triangular end of a wall beneath a pitched roof.

entries.clue: Prohibits importing German sausages (7)

indicatorNotes.importing: the prohibit word brings in the German

annotation.surface: A ban on importing German sausages.
annotation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a sausage.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang, as in 'bangers and mash', for sausages.

entries.clue: Head reads this attractive copy following tutor’s lead (8,4)

indicatorNotes.following: the copy comes after the tutor's letter

annotation.surface: A headteacher reads a pupil's charming copy after the tutor has.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Head' reads as a head teacher; it is the read head of a tape machine.
annotation.definitionFit: Magnetic tape is read by a tape head in recorders and old computers.

entries.clue: Basic meal Mike gave to wanted criminal (4,3,3,3)

indicatorNotes.criminal: the letters are treated criminally, i.e. rearranged

blocks.note: Mike = M in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: Mike gave a plain supper to a wanted criminal.
annotation.walkthrough: 'wanted criminal' reads as a fugitive; 'wanted' is fodder and 'criminal' the indicator. Meat and two veg is a British phrase for a plain dinner.
annotation.definitionFit: Meat and two veg is a plain traditional meal of meat and two vegetables.

entries.clue: Old and insensitive sort probing the unknown doctrine (8)

indicatorNotes.probing: the old insensitive sort pokes into the other pieces

blocks.note: someone as unfeeling as a log

annotation.surface: A crusty old type investigates the mysteries of doctrine.
annotation.walkthrough: O+LOG goes into THE+Y.
annotation.definitionFit: A loose synonym: the body of religious teaching a church holds is its doctrine.

entries.clue: Idiots returned to northern satellite city (3,7)

indicatorNotes.returned: the idiots word is sent back

annotation.surface: Fools come back to a northern commuter town.
annotation.walkthrough: 'satellite city' reads as a commuter town, but 'satellite' is a moon and 'city' alone is the definition. A nana is a fool in British slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a large Texan city, home of the Alamo.

entries.clue: Have control over photographic session? (4,3,5)

blocks.note: the idiom for being in charge
literally, choosing which photographs to take

annotation.surface: Someone takes charge of a photo shoot.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the literal reading of shots as photographs.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for being in charge, and literally what a director does when choosing which photos to take.

entries.clue: Grant for one when time right, no longer missing news? (10)

indicatorNotes.missing: a phrase missing something has lost it, so 'no longer' loses its Ns

blocks.note: NO LONGER without its two Ns (news = Ns)

annotation.surface: A grant paid out once the time is right, with no more waiting for news.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Grant' reads as a sum of money; it is Russell Grant, a well-known British TV astrologer. 'news' is the plural of N.
annotation.definitionFit: Russell Grant is an astrologer, famous for horoscopes on British TV.

entries.clue: Based on eight nil cup thrashing, Arsenal largely sticking to starters (5)

indicatorNotes.sticking to: the first letters stay next to the nil

blocks.note: first letters of Cup Thrashing Arsenal Largely

annotation.surface: An eight-nil cup thrashing, with Arsenal mostly relying on their starting eleven.
annotation.walkthrough: 'eight nil' reads as a score; only 'nil' is wordplay and 'Based on eight' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Octal means using base eight.

entries.clue: What some tunnellers hope to do — get by (4,4,4)

annotation.definition: What some tunnellers hope to do

blocks.clueFragment: What some tunnellers hope to do
blocks.note: diggers from both ends hope their tunnels join
the idiom for managing on little money

annotation.surface: Tunnel diggers hope to break through.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half is literal, as when the Channel Tunnel was dug from both ends.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom for managing on a tight income, taken literally for diggers joining up a tunnel.

entries.clue: Leave tense work outside of Oklahoma, as Wild West policy may have been (5-2-4)

annotation.definition: as Wild West policy may have been

indicatorNotes.outside of: the work word goes around OK

blocks.note: to till is to work the soil; split T…ILL

annotation.surface: Frontier rules outside Oklahoma, where tension was high.
annotation.walkthrough: SHOO is an order to go away, so it serves for 'Leave'.
annotation.definitionFit: A shoot-to-kill policy authorises lethal force, as a lawman in the Wild West might have had.

entries.clue: Terriers following lead of spaniels, interrupting happy Crufts hopeful? (10)

indicatorNotes.following: the terriers come after the S
indicatorNotes.interrupting: those letters break into the word for happy

blocks.note: the Territorial Army, nicknamed the Terriers

annotation.surface: Terriers trotting behind spaniels at the dog show.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Terriers' look like dogs; they are British Army volunteers, the TA. Crufts is Britain's big dog show.
annotation.definitionFit: A dog entered at Crufts, the British dog show, is a contestant.

entries.clue: Father possessed by little island demon (5)

indicatorNotes.possessed by: the father is held inside the island

blocks.note: an ait is a small river island; split A…IT

annotation.surface: A priest on a small island is possessed by a demon.
annotation.walkthrough: An ait (or eyot) is a small island in a river, especially the Thames.
annotation.definitionFit: An afrit is a powerful demon of Arabian mythology.

entries.clue: Plant, originally found on isle, brought into factory (7)

indicatorNotes.originally: first letters of the next three words

blocks.note: a mill is a factory; split MIL…L
first letters of found, on, isle

annotation.surface: A plant first found on an island is brought into a factory.
annotation.walkthrough: 'originally' applies to three words, not one.
annotation.definitionFit: Milfoil is a plant, another name for yarrow.

entries.clue: Crustacean’s tongue, shortened, thrust out briefly (9)

indicatorNotes.shortened: the tongue word is cut down
indicatorNotes.briefly: the last letter of the second word is cut

annotation.surface: A shellfish's tongue, cut short, is poked out.
annotation.walkthrough: 'tongue' reads as the body part; it means a language.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: the French name for the spiny lobster, a crustacean.

entries.clue: Deceived royal seduced by swan Romeo kept in check (3,6)

indicatorNotes.kept in: the Romeo letter is held inside the word for check

blocks.note: Queen Leda of Sparta, seduced by Zeus as a swan
to stay is to check or halt; split ST…AY
Romeo = R in the phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A queen seduced by a swan while her Romeo is kept at bay.
annotation.walkthrough: Romeo is the lover in the surface and the letter R in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: Led astray means deceived or lured into wrongdoing.

entries.clue: Get a load of Tories to tour British plant (9)

indicatorNotes.to tour: the Tories go on tour, arriving next to the British letter

blocks.note: to eye something is to get a load of it, look at it
the Tories are the political right

annotation.surface: Look at the Tories going on a tour of British gardens.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Get a load of' is slang for 'look at'; the Tories are Britain's Conservative party.
annotation.definitionFit: Eyebright is a small wild plant once used to treat eye complaints.

entries.clue: Sadly, Hyades’ daughters repeatedly align with the potential killer (6,10)

indicatorNotes.repeatedly: the daughter letter is used twice

annotation.surface: The Hyades' daughters mournfully side with a would-be murderer.
annotation.walkthrough: The Hyades were nymphs of Greek myth, which makes 'daughters' look like part of the story.
annotation.definitionFit: Deadly nightshade, or belladonna, is a highly poisonous plant.

entries.clue: Celebrated learner astral cast welcomes (3-4)

indicatorNotes.cast: the letters of astral are thrown into a new shape
indicatorNotes.welcomes: to welcome a guest is to take them in, so the shuffled letters take in the L

annotation.surface: A star-studded cast welcomes a beginner.
annotation.walkthrough: 'cast' reads as actors, fitting 'celebrated', but it is the anagram indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: Used as an adjective, it describes a line-up made entirely of famous names, hence celebrated.

entries.clue: With pen this writer reported snooker (6)

indicatorNotes.reported: a report is something spoken, so we go by how the words sound, not how they are spelt

annotation.surface: A writer describes their pen, as if reporting a snooker game.
annotation.walkthrough: 'pen' reads as a writing tool; it is an animal enclosure, a sty. 'snooker' is a verb here.
annotation.definitionFit: To snooker someone is to leave them stuck, to stymie them.

entries.clue: Wine produced by Middle Eastern country endlessly (7)

indicatorNotes.endlessly: the country loses its last letter

annotation.surface: A wine made in a Middle Eastern country without end.
annotation.walkthrough: 'produced by' reads as the maker; 'by' only places the pieces side by side.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a fortified wine named after its Atlantic island home.

entries.clue: Who had moved seat on jumbo? (6)

annotation.surface: Someone asks who changed seats on a jumbo jet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'jumbo' suggests a jumbo jet, or this Jumbo puzzle; here it is an elephant.
annotation.definitionFit: A howdah is a seat, often canopied, on an elephant's back.

entries.clue: Briton greatly amused around Champagne periodically (8)

indicatorNotes.around: the word for greatly amused is turned round

blocks.note: slew = slayed, as in 'you slay me', i.e. greatly amused

annotation.surface: A Brit much tickled by drinking champagne now and then.
annotation.walkthrough: To slay an audience is to make them laugh a lot, so SLEW is 'greatly amused'.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by category: a man from Wales is one kind of Briton.

entries.clue: What’s below zero? Anyone there? (5)

indicatorNotes.below: in a down answer, what's below zero is placed on top of the O

annotation.surface: Someone calls out into a freezing, empty place.
annotation.walkthrough: 'below zero' reads as freezing; the break is 'What's below' plus 'zero'.
annotation.definitionFit: Hello? is what you call out to ask if anyone is there.

entries.clue: Punters here in catastrophe where credit withdrawn (4)

indicatorNotes.where: points to the catastrophe as the word in which the removal happens
indicatorNotes.withdrawn: money withdrawn is taken out, so the credit letters are taken out

annotation.surface: Gamblers caught up in a financial crash where credit dried up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Punters' reads as gamblers; they are people in punts. The Isis is the Thames at Oxford, where punting is popular.
annotation.definitionFit: The Isis, the stretch of the Thames at Oxford, is a place for punting.

entries.clue: Instruction to sell red troops tanks (4,5)

indicatorNotes.tanks: the fodder tanks, i.e. collapses and is rebuilt

annotation.surface: An order goes out to sell off the Red Army's tanks.
annotation.walkthrough: 'tanks' reads as armoured vehicles; it is a verb meaning fails badly.
annotation.definitionFit: A stop order tells a broker to sell once a share falls to a set price.

entries.clue: Force was in van in Split (4)

blocks.note: to be in the van (vanguard) is to lead

annotation.surface: Troops were travelling in a van in Split, the Croatian city.
annotation.walkthrough: 'van' reads as a vehicle; it is the vanguard, the front. 'Split' is the Croatian city in the surface but slang for left.
annotation.definitionFit: Split means left in a hurry, fled.

entries.clue: Temperature in medicine bottle necessary to life (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the temperature letter goes inside the bottle

blocks.note: a vial holds medicine; split VI…AL

annotation.surface: Keeping a vital medicine bottle at the right temperature.
annotation.walkthrough: VIAL takes T inside.
annotation.definitionFit: The root sense, from Latin vita, life: essential to staying alive.

entries.clue: Plain craft rivalled UFO (3-8)

indicatorNotes.craft: the letters are crafted into a new word

annotation.surface: An aircraft over the plains was as strange as a UFO.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Plain craft' reads as an ordinary aircraft; 'Plain' means unattractive and 'craft' is the indicator.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: unattractive in looks, the sense of 'plain' as the opposite of pretty.

entries.clue: Freezing in panic in Gdansk (5)

indicatorNotes.in: the answer lies inside the next words

blocks.note: the last two letters of panic, all of in, and the first of Gdansk

annotation.surface: A freezing Baltic winter causes panic in Gdansk.
annotation.walkthrough: The letters run across three words: pan(IC IN G)dansk.
annotation.definitionFit: Icing is the freezing of ice on a surface, such as a wing.

entries.clue: Choked as fish went bad (9)

annotation.surface: Someone choked when the fish turned out to be off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Choked' reads as gagging on bad fish; it means strangled.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: strangled with a cord or wire, so choked in the violent sense.

entries.clue: Reluctant speaker’s ambition: not to exaggerate? (2,3,3,5)

blocks.note: literally, a shy speaker wants to say as little as possible

annotation.surface: A shy speaker's goal is never to overstate things.
annotation.walkthrough: The first half takes the idiom literally.
annotation.definitionFit: 'To say the least' introduces a deliberate understatement.
